newsitem.title: ISRAEL: EU envoy tells Israel Syria wants clarifications.
newsitem.headline: EU envoy tells Israel Syria wants clarifications.

text.p: A European envoy to the Middle East told Israel's defence minister on Monday that Syria wanted clarifications of the Jewish state's position on peace before it renewed suspended negotiations, the defence ministry said.
A statement from the ministry said envoy Miguel Angel Moratnios met Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai in Tel Aviv after arriving at the end of last week from Damascus.

"The envoy said he was impressed in Damascus that (President Hafez) Assad would be prepared to be committed to the peace process and the renewal of talks with Israel but he expects to hear clarifications on Israel's position," the statement said.

Syria, which wants Israel to withdraw fully from the Golan Heights Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war, had strongly condemned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu for refusing to swap the occupied Arab lands for peace.
No talks were held since Netanyahu took office last June. The former Israeli government broke off talks with Syria last March after a wave of Islamic suicide bombings in Israel.

The defence ministry quoted Mordechai as telling Moratinos: "Peace is an important value for Syria and Israel. Israel will insist that its security will be maintained at any future process in the Middle East."

Mordechai's office said he also told the envoy guerrilla attacks on Israeli troops in south Lebanon had a "negative impact" on the region. Last week three Israeli soldiers were killed by pro-Iranian Hizbollah guerrillas in Lebanon.
